findings.message: Some writes skip the service pipeline that architecture.md requires for every write (authorize → validate → write → audit → emit). revokeLapsedVersions revokes credential versions and destroys their ciphertext with no audit record. warnExpiring writes to core.event by hand with raw SQL, which is a second copy of the outbox emit. useSecret (use.ts:36) updates secrets.credential.last_used_* outside defineService. Fix: run the sweep's revocations and warnings through a defineService job service, so each revocation is audited and each event goes out through the pipeline's emit. Do the same for the last-used update, or record it as part of the audited use.
findings.scenario: Rotate a credential with a 24h grace period, then let the sweep run after the period ends → version 1's ciphertext is nulled, revoked_at is set, and core.audit_event has no row for it, so no one can tell who or what destroyed the value.

findings.message: dataKeyFor() puts a newly created data key into the process cache before the transaction that inserts its secrets.data_key row has committed. If that transaction rolls back (in putSecret, any later failure: the version insert, the audit write, event emit or idempotency settle), the cache still holds a key that no row records. For up to 5 minutes, the next putSecret calls on that instance hit the cache, seal values with that key and commit. Once the cache expires or the process restarts, dataKeyFor finds no row and wraps a new key. The committed ciphertexts can then never be opened: the credentials are lost. Fix: cache a key only after its row is known to be committed. Either create the data key in its own committed transaction, then re-read and cache it, or cache only on the path that read an existing row. Add a test where a putSecret fails after dataKeyFor, then a second putSecret succeeds, then the cache is cleared, then useSecret runs.
findings.scenario: First putSecret for a new tenant: dataKeyFor creates and caches K1, then the service rolls back (for example the audit append fails). A retry within 5 minutes seals the value with the cached K1 and commits, with no data_key row. After the cache expires, dataKeyFor creates K2 and useSecret throws a GCM auth failure. The stored credential can never be decrypted.

findings.message: The check that keeps values inside useSecret only catches the named case: the raw value, its base64 and its encodeURIComponent form, found in JSON.stringify output. It misses several variants. (1) The callback can return the Secret itself, or an object holding it: toJSON prints "[secret]", so the check passes and the caller can call reveal() later, outside useSecret, with no audit. (2) A Map, Set or class instance holding the value serialises to {} and passes. (3) Encoded forms that are not checked pass: hex, base64url, base64 of `user:${value}` (Basic auth), JSON-escaped values, and form-encoding with '+'. (4) scrubError does not scrub error.name. Fix: reject any result that contains a Secret instance, walk Maps, Sets and objects instead of relying on JSON.stringify, and widen the forms checked to hex, base64url and JSON-escaped.
findings.scenario: useSecret(job, {connector:'xero', purpose:'x'}, async (s) => s) resolves to the Secret, and the caller then calls .reveal() with no use audited. Also, useSecret(..., async (s) => new Map([['t', s.reveal()]])) hands back the raw token.

findings.message: useSecret and useValidSecrets decrypt a tenant credential for any ServiceContext and never call authorize(). putSecret, revokeSecret and listCredentials are all permission-checked, but the read of the plaintext is not. Any module code path running under a non-admin user's ui, mcp or chat context can decrypt any connector's credential, including msgraph-write ('Approved access changes only'). Fix: authorize a secrets:credential:use permission, scoped per connector and per caller kind, before load(), and throw ForbiddenError when it is refused.
findings.scenario: A module's MCP tool, called by an Employee token, calls useSecret(ctx, {connector:'msgraph-write', purpose:'x'}, fn). The value is decrypted and passed to fn with no permission check. The only trace is an audit row.

findings.message: The 30-day expiry window is hard-coded here and in the 'Expiring in 30 days' ticket label (KeyTickets.tsx:22). The sweep's warning windows come from EXPIRY_WARNING_DAYS in jobs.ts. If one copy changes, the screen and the notifications disagree. Fix: derive the UI window from Math.max(...EXPIRY_WARNING_DAYS).

The rotate form's Expires field starts empty. putSecret then writes expires_at = null over the stored expiry, so a rotation that leaves it blank silently removes the expiry and every future warning. Fix: prefill the field with the current expiry, or keep the stored expiry unless the admin clears it on purpose.
findings.scenario: An Admin rotates the Azure DevOps token (expires in 12 days) and leaves Expires blank → the row shows 'Expires: None' and the sweep never warns before the new PAT expires.

findings.message: expiry() turns the date picked on the form into 00:00 UTC at the start of that day. The credential stops working a day before most admins would expect, and earlier still in timezones east of UTC. Fix: use the end of the chosen day, or ask for the tenant's timezone.
findings.scenario: An Admin picks 'Oct 20' → useSecret throws 'expired' from Oct 20 00:00 UTC (10:00 in Sydney), while the screen still shows 'Oct 20'.

findings.message: open() takes the auth tag by slicing and never fixes its length. A ciphertext shorter than 28 bytes produces a short tag, and Node accepts truncated GCM tags unless authTagLength is set. Fix: pass { authTagLength: 16 } to createDecipheriv and reject input shorter than 28 bytes.

secrets.data_key.kms is written but never read. dataKeyFor hands any stored blob to whichever KMS is configured now. After AMAX_KMS is switched, that ends in a confusing remote failure. KmsError is also marked retryable for every status, including permanent 4xx errors (disabled or denied key), so jobs retry forever. Fix: compare row.kms with k.id and fail with a clear error when they differ, and set retryable only for 5xx and 429.
The 'Rotated in 90 days' ticket always passes note="No active credentials", even when there are active credentials. Fix: pass the note only when active.length is 0.

The Admin-only test only asserts that the h1 is not 'Connections and keys'. It still passes if sign-in fails or any other page renders. Fix: assert the 404 page, and that no credential table is in the page.

formsOf() only covers three encodings of the value: raw, standard base64 and encodeURIComponent. assertNoLeak and scrubError both rely on it, so any other encoding passes as clean. Missed variants: base64 of `id:secret`, which is how HTTP Basic auth sends client credentials (common for Xero and other OAuth token endpoints); base64url; hex; and JSON-escaped values. serialised() runs JSON.stringify, so a value that contains `"` or `\\` appears escaped and no longer matches. Fix: also check base64url, hex, the JSON-escaped form and the URLSearchParams form. For Basic auth, either give connectors a helper that registers the derived header value as a form, or check substrings of decoded base64 runs. Extend the AC-2 test to a table over these variants.
findings.scenario: useSecret(ctx, {connector:'xero'}, s => fetch(tokenUrl, {headers:{authorization:'Basic '+btoa(clientId+':'+s.reveal())}})) gets a 401. The thrown error message quotes the header. scrubError finds none of the three forms in it, so the logged error contains a Basic header that decodes to the client secret.

findings.message: putSecret accepts an expiresAt in the past. The credential is then 'expired' immediately, and the sweep emits a 'withinDays: 1' expiring warning for a credential that has already expired. Fix: reject past expiry dates in the input schema, or emit a separate expired event.
findings.scenario: Add a credential with expiresAt 2026-01-01. The page shows 'Expired', and the next sweep emits secrets.credential.expiring with withinDays 1.
